V.     The profit distribution plan or the proposal on transfer of the capital reserve fund into capital for the
       Reporting Period as approved by the Board


       The Company’s profit distribution plan for the year of 2025 is as follows: a cash dividend of RMB3.5 (tax inclusive)
       for every 10 shares will be distributed to holders of A Shares and holders of H Shares based on the total share
       capital of the Company as registered on the record date for the annual dividend distribution excluding the shares
       in the special stock account for share repurchase of the Company. On the basis of 17,513,622,829 Shares, which
       is calculated based on the total share capital of 17,628,925,829 Shares of the Company as of 31 December 2025,
       deducting 115,303,000 Shares in the special stock account for share repurchase of the Company, the total amount
       of cash dividends to be distributed would be RMB6,129,767,990 (tax inclusive). The aggregate annual cash
       dividends to be distributed by the Company, including the distributed 2025 interim cash dividends amount to
       RMB2,627,043,424 (tax inclusive), is RMB8,756,811,414 (tax inclusive). Meanwhile, in accordance with the relevant
                                                                           《上市公司股份回購規則》
       provisions of the Rules for Repurchase of Shares by Listed Companies (         ) issued by the
       CSRC, where a listed company repurchases its shares for cash consideration by means of tender offer or centralized
       bidding, such repurchases shall be deemed as cash dividends of the listed company and shall be included in the
       calculation the relevant cash dividend ratios. During the year, the amount of share repurchased by the Company
       by way of centralized bidding with the consideration in cash was RMB1,210,734,497 (excluding transaction fees).
       Accordingly, the aggregate annual cash dividends to be distributed and the amount of share repurchase totalled
       RMB9,967,545,911 (tax inclusive), representing 35.84% of the net profit attributable to equity holders of the Company
       in the consolidated financial statements for 2025 (representing 46.60% of the net profit attributable to equity holders
       of the Company after deducting non-recurring profit and loss in the consolidated financial statements for 2025).


       The Company’s profit distribution plan for the year 2025 was considered and approved at the twelfth meeting of the
       seventh session of the Board and remains subject to approval by the Shareholders at the general meeting.

X.    Major risk warning


      The risks faced by the Company in its operations mainly include: market risk, credit risk, liquidity risk, operational
      risk and reputational risk, which are specifically embodied as the risk of loss to the Company due to unfavorable
      changes of market prices; risk of loss to the Company due to failures to perform their obligations stipulated in
      relevant contracts by securities issuer, counterparties and debtors or the changes of market value of the debts
      caused by the changes of credit rating or contract performance capacity; risk of not being able to obtain sufficient
      funds in time at reasonable costs to repay debts that are due, fulfil other payment obligations and satisfy the funding
      requirements for ordinary business operation; risk of loss caused by the failures of internal systems and procedures,
      improper employee behaviors, IT risks and the influence of external events; and risk of negative evaluation of the
      Company’s reputation due to the Company’s operation, management and other activities or external events.


      The Company has established an effective internal control system, a compliance management system and
      a dynamic regulatory system based on risk control indicators to enable the operations of the Company to be
      conducted within an extent of predictable, controllable and tolerable risks.


      Investors are advised to read “Section III Management Discussion and Analysis” as set out in the Report carefully for
      risks related to the operations of the Company.

                                                                                  Chairman’s Statement




Dear Shareholders,

The year 2025 marked the conclusion of the 14th Five-Year Plan and a year of momentum building toward the 15th
Five-Year Plan. Against the backdrop of profound and complex changes in the domestic and international environment,
China ’ s economy demonstrated resilience in forging ahead under pressure and growing dynamism in pursuing
innovation-driven and higher-quality development. Comprehensive reforms on both the investment and financing sides of
the capital market were advanced in depth, significantly strengthening market resilience and vitality, with the momentum
toward stabilization and improvement further consolidated. This year was a significant year for the development of Guotai
Haitong. As the largest A+H bilateral market merger by absorption in the history of China’s capital market, we completed
the transaction closing efficiently and advanced the post-merger integration in an orderly manner. Building on the
stronger capabilities and resource endowment following the Merger, we actively served the major development strategies
of the country and Shanghai, diligently advanced the five priority areas in finance (known as “Five Major Areas” (金融五
篇大文章), including Sci-Tech Finance, Green Finance, Inclusive Finance, Pension Finance, and Digital Finance) and
focused on improving the quality and efficiency of operation and management. We achieved historic highs in both asset
scale and operating performance, initially achieving the effect of “1+1>2”. By the end of 2025, our consolidated total assets
exceeded RMB2.1 trillion, and net assets attributable to owners of the Group reached RMB330.4 billion, both ranking first
in the industry, which demonstrating our strong and robust capital strength. Operating revenue reached RMB63.1 billion,
net profit attributable to equity holders of the Company reached RMB27.8 billion and net profit attributable to equity
holders of the Company after deducting non-recurring profit and loss amounted to RMB21.4 billion. Multiple business
metrics, including brokerage business revenue, equity and fund trading volume, margin financing and securities lending
balances, IPO underwriting, and the number of IPOs under review at year-end, ranked first in the industry, demonstrating
our professional and comprehensive service capabilities. With our industry-leading compliance and risk management
capabilities, we maintained the highest international credit rating among Chinese securities firms and has been
successfully included in major indices such as the CSI A500 Index, SSE 50 Index, FTSE China A50 Index, and FTSE China
50 Index, reflecting our intensive and efficient operational management.
                                                                                                         ANNUAL REPORT 2025     1
    Chairman’s Statement

    We remain committed to serving the country through finance and enhancing the quality and efficiency of the
    real economy. Placing functionality at the forefront, the Group maintained firmly focused on its core responsibilities and
    continued to deepen its commitment to its core business, advancing the “Five Major Areas” with solid and substantive
    results, and achieving a leap in its ability to serve national strategies and support the real economy. We demonstrated
    the empowerment of financial technology by strengthening the linkage between our business segment of investment,
    investment banking, investment research, providing full chain and full-lifecycle financial services for science and
    technology innovation enterprises, and facilitating the development of the new quality productive forces (新質生產力).
    The Group has cumulatively built a matrix of science and technology innovation-focused funds with an aggregate size of
    nearly RMB70 billion. New investments in advanced and frontier technologies exceeded RMB6 billion, while the Group
    supported equity financing of nearly RMB44 billion for 36 technology driven and innovation-focused enterprises. Our
    IPO business in both STAR Market and ChiNext continued to maintain its leading position in the industry. The Group
    maintained a market-leading position and an exemplary role in green finance, systematically improved its
    green financial service capabilities across “financing, investment, trading, cross-border and risk control”. Its green bond
    underwriting volume ranked second in the industry, and the cumulative trading volume in its carbon finance business
    reached nearly 100 million tons. MSCI ESG rating remained at the highest AAA level globally among peers. Inclusive
    finance continued to expand in both scale and coverage, alongside accelerated progress in the transformation of
    wealth management. The average monthly active users of retail customer service platform ranked first in the industry on
    a consolidated basis. The Group ranked among the top three in the industry in terms of underwriting scale of inclusive-
    themed bonds such as the Small and Micro Enterprises bonds and rural revitalization bonds. Pension finance of the
    Group gathered strong momentum built on years of sustained effort. The Group continued to enrich its products
    and services offering. Assets under management in the Group’s pension business exceeded RMB800 billion, while its
    coverage of individual pension products offered for distribution remained at an industry-leading level. We accelerated
    the advancement of digital finance and firmly moved towards “SMART Investment Banking”, enhanced capabilities in
    “Online, Data-Based and Intelligent” development level, and promoted the building of a first-class new asset management
    service platform with Chinese characteristics.


    We adhere to the principle of “customer first” and strive to improve the level of comprehensive financial
    services. Based on customer needs, we optimized and upgraded three major customer service systems, and initially
    achieved incremental expansion, quality and efficiency improvement in customer operation, with our business indicators
    hit a number of historical highs. Our retail customer service system is classified and layered, and our dual-drive
    approach of asset allocation and transaction services have achieved initial results. We ranked first in the industry in
    terms of both the number of retail clients served and the market share in brokerage services, with our leading advantage
    continuing to expand and the assets under management and the asset allocation volumes growing rapidly. Our
    institutional customer service system was intensively developed, and our “1+N” comprehensive business model
    was further promoted. We ranked first in the industry in terms of revenue from institutional trading access and execution
    services. The scale of our QFI business grew significantly, the asset custody and fund services business maintained a
    leading position, the construction of the “one institute, one academy (一所一院)” research system started steadily, and the
    ranking of our research on core customers reached a record high. Our corporate customer service system was open
    and coordinated, and the “Investment Banking+” ecosystem was continuously improved. Our IPO underwriting business
    maintained its leading position in the industry, the market share of refinancing underwriting increased significantly, the
    scale of bond underwriting reached a record high, and the synergies of financial leasing and pledge financing businesses
    were gradually released.



2   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
                                                                                  Chairman’s Statement

We embrace the wave of “going global” and work to enhance connectivity across capital markets. Positioning
as an important “connector” of high-level opening-up, the Group continues to improve our comprehensive cross-border
financial service capabilities, and steadily strengthens its influence in global capital allocation and asset pricing. We
consolidated our competitive advantages in international business and built a one-stop wealth management
platform for global assets, proactively addressing the clients’ diversified wealth management needs, with margin financing
balances recording notable growth. By seizing strategic opportunities arising from the restructuring of global industrial and
supply chains, we have better provided services for both “Investment from China” and “Investment in China”. The Group
ranked first in the industry in terms of the number of Hong Kong stock placement mandates underwritten, and topped
the list of Chinese securities companies in terms of the number of offshore bond underwriting deals for Chinese issuers.
We have advanced our overseas business deployment in a prudent and steady manner, continuously optimizing
a global service network covering 17 countries and regions with a focus on “expanding our reach” in key areas such as
Southeast Asia. Progress has been made in an orderly manner on the proposed acquisition of an Indonesian securities
firm by the overseas subsidiary. We have optimized cross-border synergy mechanisms, strengthened the efficient
integration of “two markets and two resources,” and actively supported clients’ cross-border asset allocation and business
expansion to better meet the diverse investment and financing needs of global clients. The integrated development of
cross-border investment banking and trading achieved significant results. By advancing cross-border leasing projects to
support the global expansion of “Made in China,” our capabilities to facilitate both “going global” and “bringing in” have
continued to strengthen.


We strengthened the “empowerment with digital intelligence” and deepened our leading fintech practice.
We remained firmly committed to the transformation toward a “SMART Investment Bank” in order to lead the securities
industry in achieving innovation and breakthroughs in intelligent application, and transform cutting-edge technology
into an internal driving force for business growth. We drove business transformation with innovative applications,
implemented “All in AI” strategy and built a trusted and controllable “1+N” large model technology architecture and
became the first in the industry to obtain regulatory approval for large model-powered customer service. We were the first
in the industry to launch the new-generation fully AI-powered intelligent App Lingxi (靈犀), which has been upgraded
into version 2.0, realizing all-scenario and large-scale application of large models in various business areas. We supported
integration with our technical strengths, and leveraged on our accumulated advanced technology capabilities to
successfully implement the legal entity transition, successfully complete the customer migration, and completed the
customer system restructuring with the largest customer scale and the fastest execution in the industry, providing a
benchmark industry practice for system integration and upgrading. We built a digital ecosystem with smart platforms,
and completed the establishment of an enterprise-level database. We upgraded OneLink, an integrated digital and
intelligent business development platform, to enhance service capabilities, release synergies, and vigorously promote the
platform-based, digital and intelligent, and centralized operations.




                                                                                                         ANNUAL REPORT 2025     3
    Chairman’s Statement

    We emphasize on the principle of “putting righteousness first” and actively shoulder the social responsibility of
    a state-owned financial institution. We adhere to the long-term approach in practicing ESG philosophy, strive to be the
    vanguard and forerunner of “Serving the Country with Finance” and “Finance for Good”. We have firmly reinforced our
    commitment to shareholders’ return, constantly enhancing the stability, sustainability and predictability of dividends,
    and carried out interim dividends for the second consecutive year. The total annual dividends reached RMB8.8 billion,
    and the dividend ratio ranked among the top tier of the leading securities firms. The Group repurchased RMB1.2 billion
    of the Company’s A Shares by way of centralized bidding, which effectively protected shareholders’ interests and boosted
    market confidence. We take the initiative to assume corporate citizenship responsibility, focusing on areas such
    as supporting people-cantered urban development, participating in emergency disaster relief, and advocating volunteer
    services. We actively carried out various public welfare activities, deepened the paired assistance work of “headquarter-
    branch-county (一總一分一縣)”, and supported the comprehensive rural revitalization with concrete actions. Since the
    foundation was established in 2012, we have donated over RMB570 million in aggregate and have helped 10 national-level
    poverty-stricken counties get out of poverty. We comprehensively promoted cultural integration and renewal, fully
    implemented the requirements of a financial culture with Chinese characteristics, and established a new cultural concept
    system. Adhering to the corporate philosophy of “compliance and integrity, steady and long-term development”, and “long-
    term partnership and mutual benefit”, we empower high-quality development with culture, and have been awarded the
    highest rating by the assessment of industrial culture construction practice for five consecutive years.


    We have already achieved significant accomplishments in the past and will make further progress in the
    near future. The “15th Five-Year Plan” period will be a critical stage for advancing Chinese-style modernisation and
    accelerating the building of China into a leading financial powerhouse. It will also be a pivotal period for comprehensively
    deepening capital market reforms and expediting the development of first-class investment banks. In the face of new
    circumstances and requirements, we have formulated a new three-year strategic plan based on overall situation and
    by benchmarking against world-class standards. The plan clearly defines our development goal of “leading the overall
    domestic market with internationally recognized excellence”. The year 2026 marks a pivotal year for Guotai Haitong to
    embark on a new three-year strategic plan and deepen its post-merger integration and development. We will capitalize
    on the momentum of times and forge ahead with determination. Anchored by our vision of “becoming a first-class
    investment bank with international competitiveness and market leadership,” we will remain mindful of our position as
    a “leading market institution”. We will stay closely aligned with our main objective of serving national strategies and the
    real economy, seize the opportunities presented by the comprehensive and deep reforms of capital market, and take
    the implementation of new strategies and corporate culture as an opportunity to advance integration and synergy in
    depth. We will comprehensively upgrade the service level by optimizing the synergy and linkage mechanism, and take
    the continuous deepening of reform and innovation as an opportunity to stimulate endogenous growth momentum. We
    will actively advance the “Five Major Areas”, striving to become a “service provider” of direct financing, a “gatekeeper” of
    the capital market, and a “manager” of social wealth, and contribute greater strength to Chinese modernization and the
    development of China into a leading financial power.

     VI. OTHER INFORMATION OF THE COMPANY

           (I) History of the Company, mainly including the reform and restructuring, capital injections
               in the previous years

                 In August 1999, with the approval of the CSRC, Guotai Securities Co., Ltd. merged with J&A Securities Co.,
                 Ltd. The shareholders of Guotai Securities Co., Ltd. and J&A Securities Co., Ltd. and other investors jointly
                 established the Company, with a registered capital of RMB3,727.18 million.


                 In December 2001, with the approval of the CSRC, the Company was split into two companies with
                 independent legal status by way of split-off. The Company, as the continuing company, owned and undertook
                 the securities businesses related assets, businesses and liabilities relating to such assets and businesses. The
                 registered capital of the Company changed to RMB3.7 billion.




10   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
         Section II Company Profile and Key Financial Indicators

    In January 2006, with the approval of the CSRC, Central Huijin Investment Ltd. (中央匯金投資有限責任公
    司) subscribed for 1 billion additional Shares of the Company and thus the registered capital of the Company
    changed to RMB4.7 billion.


    In March 2012, with the approval of the Shanghai Bureau of the CSRC, the Company issued 1.4 billion
    additional Shares and thus the registered capital changed to RMB6.1 billion.


    In June 2015, with the approval of the CSRC, the Company issued 1,525 million A Shares through initial public
    offering, which were listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on 26 June 2015 and thus the registered capital
    changed to RMB7,625 million.


    In April 2017, with the approval of the CSRC and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the Company issued 1,040
    million H Shares, and the Company issued 48.9338 million additional H Shares upon the exercise of the
    overallotment option in May 2017, and thus the registered capital changed to RMB8,713.9338 million.


    In April 2019, the Company completed the placing of 194 million H Shares under a general mandate and thus
    the registered capital changed to RMB8,907.947954 million.


    In March 2025, with the approval of the CSRC and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the Company merged
    with Haitong Securities by way of share exchange and absorption through the issuance of 5,985,871,332 A
    Shares to all A share-exchange shareholders of Haitong Securities (treasury shares were also involved in
    the exchange) and the issuance of 2,113,932,668 H Shares to all H share-exchange shareholders of Haitong
    Securities. And the Company issued 626,174,076 A Shares to Shanghai SA to raise ancillary funds of RMB10
    billion (the “Placing” or the “Placing of A Shares”). On 3 April 2025, The Chinese name and English name of the
    Company was changed to “ 國泰海通證券股份有限公司” and “GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.”
    respectively, and the registered capital was changed to RMB17,629,708,696.

     Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

     I.    BUSINESSES OF THE COMPANY DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD

           Driven by customer demand, the Group has established a retail, institutional and corporate customer service system,
           forming the business segments covering wealth management business, investment banking business, institution
           and transaction business, investment management business and finance lease business. The principal profit model
           of the Group is to generate fee and commission income and interest income through provision of financial products
           or services for clients and receive investment gains through securities or equity investments.


           In terms of specific businesses:


           Our wealth management business mainly provides securities and futures brokerage, financial products, investment
           advisory, margin financing and securities lending, stock pledging, agreed securities repurchase and other services to
           clients.


           Our investment banking business mainly provides listing sponsorship, equity underwriting, debt underwriting,
           structured debt financing, M&A financial advisory and diversified corporate solutions to corporate and government
           clients.


           Our institution and transaction business mainly consists of research, institutional services, trading and investment
           and alternative investment. Among which, institutional services mainly provides integrated financial service,
           including prime brokers, seat leasing, asset allocation, custody and outsourcing, and trading services to domestic and
           overseas institutional clients; trading and investment business mainly includes investment transactions in stocks,
           fixed income, foreign exchange, large commodities and their derivative financial instruments, as well as provision of
           integrated financial solutions for clients’ investment, financing and risk management.


           Our investment management business provides fund management and asset management services to institutions,
           enterprises and individuals.


           Our finance lease business mainly provides innovative financial service solutions, including finance lease, operating
           lease and relevant consultancy and other services to individuals, enterprises and government clients.

3.   Institution and transaction business

     Market Environment

     In 2025, following the promulgation of the new National Nine Articles, together with the effective rollout
     of the comprehensive “1+N” policy framework for the capital market, China’s capital market experiences
     a systematic reshaping spanning from institutional foundations to market ecosystem, fortifying the
     market’ s resilience against risks, and markedly improving investor confidence and expectations.
     A-share indices registered gains and the aggregate market capitalisation of A-share market surpassed
     RMB100 trillion for the first time in history. Internationally, the US equity market sustained its upward
     trajectory, while the Hong Kong stock market exhibited robust performance. The Fixed Income,
     Currency, and Commodities (FICC) market experienced divergent trends. The domestic bond market
     remained relatively subdued, the US government bonds fluctuated within broad ranges, gold and other
     precious metals repeatedly attained new record highs, and the US dollar index retreated. The year
     2025 also represents a pivotal milestone in the reconfiguration of the institutional investor ecosystem,
     characterised by the rapid influx of medium and long-term capital into the market and an accelerated
     evolution of the capital market towards institutionalisation and internationalisation, propelling the
     institutional business segment into a new era of strategic opportunities.

64   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
          Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

As of 31 December 2025, the Group’s total assets amounted to RMB2,114.338 billion, representing an
increase of 101.80% compared with the end of last year; total liabilities amounted to RMB1,768.135
billion, representing an increase of 103.17% compared with the end of last year; and total equity
amounted to RMB346.203 billion, representing an increase of 95.07% compared with the end of last
year. The Group’s gearing ratio as of 31 December 2025 was 78.36% representing an increase of 0.67
percentage point compared with the end of last year. The Group has a reasonable debt structure no
overdue outstanding debts, sound operating performance, strong profitability, and excellent long-term
and short-term debt repayment capabilities.


The Group’s asset structure is mainly as follows: financial assets at fair value through profit or loss
amounted to RMB688.563 billion, accounting for 32.57% of total assets; cash held on behalf of brokerage
clients amounted to RMB416.419 billion, accounting for 19.69% of total assets; margin accounts
receivable amounted to RMB253.572 billion, accounting for 11.99% of total assets; debt instruments at
fair value through other comprehensive income amounted to RMB145.669 billion, accounting for 6.89%
of total assets; and refundable deposits amounted to RMB121.709 billion, accounting for 5.76% of total
assets. Among these, current assets amounted to RMB1,681.579 billion, accounting for 79.53% of total
assets. The Group’s assets have good liquidity and a reasonable structure. Furthermore, considering
the impact of market volatility, the Group has made corresponding impairment provisions for assets
showing signs of impairment, maintaining high asset quality.


Non-current assets


As of 31 December 2025, non-current assets amounted to RMB432.760 billion, representing an increase
of 118.01% compared with the end of last year, mainly due to the Merger with Haitong Securities by
way of absorption. Among them, refundable deposits amounted to RMB121.709 billion, representing
an increase of 85.80% compared with the end of last year; equity instruments at fair value through other
comprehensive income amounted to RMB65.019 billion, representing an increase of 203.90% compared
with the end of last year, mainly due to the Merger with Haitong Securities by way of absorption and the
increase in the scale of non-trading equity investments; and receivables arising from sale and leaseback
arrangements amounted to RMB36.053 billion, mainly due to the new leasing business resulting from
the Merger with Haitong Securities by way of absorption.


Current assets


As of 31 December 2025, current assets amounted to RMB1,681.579 billion, representing an increase of
98.01% compared with the end of last year, mainly due to the Merger with Haitong Securities by way of
absorption. Among them, financial assets at fair value through profit or loss amounted to RMB657.923
billion, representing an increase of 65.98% compared with the end of last year; cash held on behalf of
brokerage customers amounted to RMB416.419 billion, representing an increase of 105.57% compared
with the end of last year; and margin accounts receivable amounted to RMB253.572 billion, representing
an increase of 138.61% compared with the end of last year.

                           On 14 March 2025, the Company completed the Closing of the Merger transaction. Pursuant to the

                           and initiated various works at the earliest opportunity. Up to now, the Company has realized the stable

70   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
           Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

Prioritising customers, ensuring smooth business integration, and comprehensively assuming
qualifications and business activities. The Company promptly completed the replacement of
business licenses for both the parent company and its nationwide branches, seamlessly inherited all
requisite licenses, qualifications and business quotas, and achieved uninterrupted succession of various
business agreements. The principal assets involved in the transaction were duly transferred, ensuring
the continuous and stable operation of all businesses. The Company comprehensively unified
customer services through systematically aligning the original customer service systems of the two
companies, and unifying the appropriateness management, service standards, business processes and
system platform for various customers including retail, institutional and corporate customers in a timely
and effective manner. The interconnection of customer accounts was achieved, enabling the delivery
of consistent, reliable and stable service experience to all clients. The Company refreshed the client-
facing brand image by launching the omni-channel platforms including the new official website, the
new official WeChat account and APP, marking the commencement of business operations under the
new name and presenting a unified and refreshed brand image to the market. The integration and
development of subsidiaries was advanced in an orderly manner, with in-depth research and
analysis conducted to address issues such as inter-subsidiary competition and ensure compliance
with the “one participation, one control” (一參一控) regulatory requirement, and integration of asset
management subsidiaries initiated as a first step.


Prioritizing risk control and effectively achieving unified management. The Company unified
the compliance, risk control and financial and asset-liability management through taking the lead in
formulating the integrated compliance and risk control plan, updating over 700 internal policies, unifying
the compliance management, risk policies, authorization frameworks and regulatory reporting standards,
strengthening the oversight of subsidiaries, and effectively mitigating overseas risk exposures. The
Company completed the unification of human resources management and the restructuring of
its organizational structure by consolidating and establishing 7 business or management committees,
41 headquarter departments and 44 branch offices. Key management appointments and alignment
of position-to-personnel were completed swiftly, ensuring the smooth transition of employee labor
contracts and harmonization of job grades and compensation. The Company refreshed its strategic
planning and cultural framework by organizing the formulation of a new strategic planning system
with a clear development objective of “comprehensive leading in China and distinctive and outstanding
in the world”, established a corporate cultural concept grounded in the shared values of “Serving the
Country with Finance and Finance for Good” and further strengthened internal cohesion and unity
of purpose. The Company achieved the integration of workplace and property management
by facilitating the relocation of workplace in phases while simultaneously completing the property
management integration and positioning optimization. The internal management system was launched
successfully, enabling the centralised utilization and sharing of office resources.

                       Adhering to systematic planning and successfully completing the system transition. In
                       September 2025, the Company successfully implemented the legal entity transition, achieving
                       a 45% business switching plan that is an innovative breakthrough compared with previous cases in the
                       industry, and significantly reduced the affected business scope and duration; after the transition, the
                       legal entities on China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited (the "CSDCC") and
                       its Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen Branches, the SSE, SZSE and BSE, the National Equities Exchange
                       and Quotations, China Securities Investor Protection Fund Corporation Limited, the 21 contracted
                       depository banks, and Shanghai Gold Exchange were switched to Guotai Haitong, successfully realizing
                       the operation of a single entity. In January 2026, the Company successfully completed the
                       migration of customers and business (i.e. internal handover), realized the integration of hundreds
                       of IT systems, and completely migrated the data of over 20 million customers and relevant business
                       of the former Haitong Securities to the mature next-generation distributed core trading system of the
                       Company through 21 batches. After the transition, the Company’s core trading system has carried nearly
                       40 million customers, becoming the full-stack innovation-driven, core trading system with the largest
                       customer scale in the industry, and had withstood the test of the pressure of the huge amount of market
                       transactions, effectively laying a solid foundation for future development.

(V) The situation of structured entities controlled by the Company

    schemes, investment funds and limited partnerships. For funds or asset management plans where the Group
    acts as manager or holder, and for partnerships where it serves as general partner or investment manager,
    the Group determined that it exercises control over certain funds, asset management plans, and partnerships

    variable returns. These entities were consequently included in the scope of consolidation. As of 31 December
    2025, the aforementioned structured entities included in the consolidation scope contributed RMB6.594

     VI. DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF THE COMPANY ON ITS FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

           (I) Industry landscape and trend

                 In recent years, the industry structure has been continuously optimized, with landmark restructuring
                 transactions being smoothly implemented. Leading companies have played an increasingly prominent role,
                 while small and medium-sized institutions have achieved breakthroughs by focusing on niche segments,
                 and foreign institutions have accelerated the expansion of their domestic operations. Against this backdrop,
                 the securities industry strengthens its functional responsibilities and missions, continuously enhance its
                 professional service capabilities and globalization level, and has demonstrated more clearly development
                 trend of service integration, differentiated competition, international expansion and digital and intelligent
                 operations.


                 1.    Service integration


                       After more than three decades of reform and development, China’s capital market has entered a new
                       stage of building a modern capital market with Chinese characteristics. With the ongoing deepening of
                       capital market reform and the continuous accumulation of household wealth, the traditional business
                       models of securities firms are in urgent need of transformation and innovation. At the same time,
                       other financial institutions, such as banks and insurance companies, are penetrating into the securities
                       business by leveraging their own advantages, which posed challenges to the comprehensive service
                       capabilities of securities firms. In the future, in order to adapt to changing customer needs and evolving
                       competitive environment, securities companies will continue to expand the depth and breadth of
                       business and services, and pursue integration across business lines, products, channels, and support
                       service systems to transform into comprehensive financial service providers with complete business,
                       industrial and service chains. This marks a shift from a passive channel provider to enterprise partner,
                       product creator, risk manager, and value explorer.




80   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
               Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

2.   Differentiated competition


     In recent years, with the deepening of marketization and increasingly intense competition, China's
     securities industry has gradually transformed from homogenization, ragmentation and channel-driven
     toward differentiation, consolidation and specialization, with capital, profits and core business market
     shares concentrated among top securities companies. The increasingly intensifying market competition
     and the rapid development of innovative business have imposed higher requirements on the capital
     strength, talent reserves and risk management capabilities of securities companies, while also opening
     up broader development space. As a result, the industry is increasingly exhibiting clear trends of
     business differentiation and the concentration of high-quality resources to leading securities companies.
     The National “15th Five-Year” Plan proposal advocates for “promoting financial institutions to focus
     on their core businesses, improve governance, and pursue differentiated development”. The CSRC has
     set forth the objective that “establish two or three investment banks and institutions with international
     competitiveness and market leadership by 2035”. Looking ahead, top securities companies will continue
     to expand their scale and enhance their strength through both organic growth and external development,
     thereby consolidating their competitive advantages across the entire market and all business segments
     to achieve comprehensive leadership. Meanwhile, small and medium-sized securities companies
     without comprehensive strength are expected to concentrate their advantageous resources and other
     favourable conditions to develop competitive advantages in specific niche business areas or regional
     markets, forming a differentiated and multi-tiered competitive landscape alongside top securities
     companies.




                                                                                           ANNUAL REPORT 2025    81
     Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

                 3.    Globalization development


                       With the further comprehensive deepening of reforms and the continuous optimization of the opening
                       up system, the PRC capital market and securities industry has continued to expand its high-level
                       systematic opening-up and accelerated to introduce and implement various opening-up measures.
                       The system for overseas listing and financing of enterprises has been continuously improved, the scope
                       of stock connect has gradually expanded, the international product system has become increasingly
                       diverse and the cooperation between domestic and overseas markets has continued to deepen. In
                       this process, the internationalization level of the PRC securities industry has further improved, more
                       and more domestic securities firms are intensifying their efforts to expand overseas markets through
                       branches establishment, business cooperation, and mergers and acquisitions. Particularly, they are
                       enhancing branches establishment and team layouts in regions along the “Belt and Road”, to provide
                       comprehensive cross-border investment and financing services for global institutional investors and
                       domestic and foreign industrial clients. In the future, the high-level two-way opening of the capital
                       market will be further deepened and the convenience of cross-border investment and financing
                       will be further improved, which will bring more diverse cross-border business scenarios and service
                       tools and more opportunities for the international development of securities firms. At the same time,
                       securities companies are also required to make forward-looking layouts in various aspects such as
                       license qualifications, system construction, customer acquisition, product reserves and capacity
                       building to strengthen cross-border integrated risk control and business collaboration. Among them,
                       leading securities companies have the greater potential to grow into large-scale investment banks with
                       international competitiveness by allocating resources, serving customers and managing risks globally.


                 4.    Digital and intelligent operations


                       Advanced digital and intelligent technologies have profoundly transformed the operating environment
                       and competitive landscape of the securities industry. In response to the penetration of the internet
                       and the new wave of revolution brought about by large models, securities firms have increased their
                       investment in information technology. Advanced digital technologies have been used to enhance
                       customer experience, optimize business processes, improve operational efficiency and reduce the cost
                       of risk, which has supported the transformation of China's securities companies’ business operations
                       from the traditional fee-based approaches towards a diversified model focusing on professional services,
                       deepening customer relationships and leveraging online services. In recent years, the top-level layout
                       and planning of China's digital economy have been continuously refined. The “science and technology
                       finance” and “digital finance” proposed by Central Economic Work Conference have also set clear
                       requirements for the development of financial technology and digital and intelligent transformation of
                       the securities industry. In order to enhance the capabilities for serving real economy and improve their
                       own development quality, securities companies must further strengthen their digital intellectualization of
                       business thinking, positioning digital intellectualization technology as a key driver of transformation. By
                       fully leveraging advanced technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence, securities companies
                       are set to drive organisational transformation, process innovation, and the upgrading of business models,
                       which will significantly enhance overall operational efficiency and foster the development of a top-down,
                       digitally driven strategic synergy, thereby providing investors with more intelligent, personalized and
                       precise products and services, and better serving the real economy.

           (IV) Possible risk exposure

                 The global economy has entered a period of profound adjustment, marked by intertwined transformations
                 and challenges. Geopolitical conflicts continue to intensify, coupled with the restructuring of global supply
                 chains and a rise in sovereign debt risks across multiple countries, resulting in significantly increased volatility
                 in international financial markets. Despite these headwinds, China’s economy demonstrated strong resilience
                 under pressure, with GDP growth meeting expectations, overall employment remaining stable, foreign trade
                 growing rapidly, export diversification yielding notable progress, new quality productive forces developing
                 steadily and risks in key areas being solved effectively. However, the complex evolution of both domestic and
                 external environments has given rise to a range of risks and challenges, which warrant heightened vigilance.
                 In terms of market risk, the expansion of derivatives, commodities, and foreign exchange operations, coupled
                 with the normalisation of two-way fluctuations in the RMB exchange rate, posed greater challenges to business
                 operations. In terms of credit risk, as China’s economy has been undergoing profound transformation,
                 financing-related businesses and fixed-income investments require continued attention on structural issues
                 in sectors such as real estate, local debt, and small and medium-sized financial institutions. The Company
                 will remain steadfast in its commitment to prudent operations, continuously enhance its comprehensive risk
                 management system, and strengthen its forward-looking risk assessment and early warning capabilities, so as
                 to achieve both qualitative enhancement and reasonable quantitative growth.


           (V) Risk Management

                 1.    Overview


                       In 2025, the Company adhered to the principle of “compliance and risk control first” in the process of
                       merger and integration to comprehensively promote the in-depth integration and systematic upgrading
                       of its risk management system and strive to establish a comprehensive risk management system that
                       aligns with the Company’s new development stage. The Company has established a sound corporate
                       governance structure and maintained standardized and orderly operation. The shareholders’ general
                       meetings and the Board have exercised their functions and powers in strict accordance with the
                       provisions of the Company Law, the Securities Law and the Articles of Association, and performed
                       scientific decision-making and effective supervision on significant operational matters, effectively
                       ensuring the independence, transparency and scientific decision-making of corporate governance.

The company has consistently adhered to the principle of prudent operation, guided by the philosophy
that “risk management creates value ”. It has established and continuously refined a four-tier risk
management framework, solidifying three lines of defence: frontline prevention and control, dedicated
risk management, and internal audit supervision. The Company has ostered a risk management culture
involving all employees and enhanced the collaborative and synergy mechanism across all units and
levels, thereby promoting the in-depth integration of and dynamic balance between risk management
and business development and continuously improving the Group ’ s overall capabilities in risk
identification, measurement, monitoring, and response.


The Company has implemented a unified risk appetite system to improve hierarchical authorization
and centralized limit control, strengthen risk management for the same business and same customer,
and continuously enhance risk penetration capabilities. Focusing on market, credit, liquidity,

mechanism to realize dynamic identification and categorised responses. Through business guidance,
operational support and decision management, the Company applies differentiated yet standardised
vertical risk management to its subsidiaries to ensure the effective transmission of the Group’s policies.
The Company has established a normalized early warning and forecasting mechanism by closely
monitoring changes in the external environment with focuses on key businesses and critical areas. Multi-
dimensional early warning indicators and tiered response thresholds have been set, which, along with
stress testing and scenario analysis, have continuously enhanced the sensitivity of risk alerts and the
forward-looking nature of risk responses. The Company incorporated innovative business operations
and ESG risk factors into its comprehensive risk management system, establishing corresponding
decision-making mechanisms, management protocols, and comprehensive risk control processes.
Through conducting risk identification and assessment, as well as compliance reviews, the Company
ensures that risks are measurable, controllable, and within acceptable limits.


The Company has increased its investment in information technology in respect of compliance and risk
management, and accelerated the promotion of digital and intelligent transformation of the Group ’s
risk control. By optimizing and upgrading the integrated risk management platform, strengthening the
centralized collection and unified management of risk data, and deepening the integration and sharing
of internal and external information, the Company has further improved its digital and intelligent
support capability for risk monitoring, early warning and reporting. Meanwhile, the Company has
actively explored the application of new technologies such as artificial intelligence and big data in
risk identification, evaluation and analysis, as well as early warning and response, thereby constantly
improving the depth and intelligence of risk insight.

                             The Risk Control Committee is delegated by the Board to perform part of its comprehensive
                             risk management duties. The Audit Committee is responsible for supervising comprehensive
                             risk management to oversee and review the performance of the Board and management in risk

3.   Measures against various risks


     (1)   Market risks


           Market risks are those that may cause loss to the Company due to unfavorable changes of
           market prices, which include but are not limited to interest rates, exchange rates, stock prices
           and commodity prices. The businesses of the Company that involve market risks mainly include
           the transactions and investment of equity securities and their derivatives, the transactions and
           investment of fixed-income securities and their derivatives as well as transactions such as foreign
           exchange transactions, precious metal transactions and commodity transactions.


           The Company implements a limit-based management for market risks and formulates a market
           risk limit system comprising business scale, loss limit, Value at Risk (VaR), exposure, Greek letters,
           effectiveness of hedge and concentration, as well as various types of risk indicators. It determines
           the alarm standards, warning standards and responding measures for market risks. The Company
           conducts daily monitoring for market risk limits by using its risk management system to monitor
           the operation of its businesses, reports on market risk oversight and management conditions,
           and performs specialized analysis on risk matters, in order to provide basis for decision making.
           The Company adopts methods such as Value at Risk (VaR) and stress tests to analyze and assess
           market risk. The Company’s Value at Risk (VaR) calculation applies a historical simulation method
           based on historical data for the previous 12 months, assuming the holding period is one day and
           the confidence level is 95%. The calculation model of VaR covers equity price risk, interest rate risk,
           commodity price risk and exchange rate risk. The Company regularly reviews the effectiveness of
           the VaR model through the back testing method.

(2)   Credit risks


      Credit risks are those that may cause a loss to the Company due to failures to perform their
      obligations stipulated in relevant contracts by securities issuers, counterparties and debtors
      or the changes of market value of the debts caused by the changes of credit rating or contract
      performance capacity. The Company’s current credit risks mainly concentrate on the bond
      investment business, margin financing and securities lending business, stock-pledged repurchase
      transaction business and OTC derivatives business.


      The Company enforces admission control for credit risk, by which credit rating assessments
      will be made on the clients before engaging in credit risk-related activities and only those who
      meet the admission criteria are eligible for grant of credit and business engagement. Each
      business department shall conduct due diligence based on the actual circumstances of the
      business engagement, make an assessment on credit worthiness of the clients, and determine the
      corresponding transaction limits.


      The Company implements measures including collecting margins, accepting qualified collateral,
      and utilizing net settlement to mitigate credit risk. Admission standards are established for bond
      investment activities, incorporating whitelist management and concentration controls, while
      also consistently monitoring and assessing credit risks of the bonds in position. Credit business
      department sets detailed admission standards and discount rates for collaterals according to
      the characteristics of their specific business. The credit risk faced by OTC derivatives business
      mainly refers to the counterparty default risk faced in carrying out OTC derivatives business such
      as forwards, swaps and options. The counterparties of OTC derivatives transactions are mainly
      financial institutions and other professional institutions. The Company manages counterparties
      credit risk by conducting qualification screening of counterparties, monitoring market fluctuations
      daily, implementing margin calls, and resorting to forced liquidation if necessary.


      The Company conducts regular reviews on the admission standards and discount rates, and
      performs ad hoc review on the event of significant market or policy changes, or material credit
      events related to counterparties. The Company manages non-cash collateral through market
      monitoring and assesses the valuation of pledged collateral. The Company analyzes credit
      risk factors across various business operations, identifying potential credit risk vulnerabilities,
      and conducts concentrated management and quantitative evaluation of credit risk. Credit risk
      management for major clients is implemented within the concentration risk control objectives.
      Analytical methods such as concentration levels, default probability, default loss rate, credit risk
      exposure and collateral coverage ratio are adopted in credit risk measurement. The Company sets
      the reasonable credit risk stress scenarios, conducts stress testing, and analyzes the test results.




                                                                                          ANNUAL REPORT 2025   91
     Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

                             As at the end of 2025, the Company’s credit risk was generally controllable, and there was no new

                             guarantee ratio for clients with outstanding liabilities in margin financing and securities lending
                             business maintained at 276.97%.


                      (3)   Liquidity risks


                             Liquidity risk refers to the risk that the Company may not be able to obtain sufficient funds in
                             a timely manner and at a reasonable cost or price to meet debts that become due, fulfill other
                             payment obligations, and satisfy funding needs for normal business operations.


                             The Company primarily adopts the risk indicator analysis methods to assess its overall liquidity
                             risk. This involves analyzing key indicators such as liquidity coverage ratio, net stable funding ratio,
                             cash flow maturity gap, net size of cash management pool, liquidity reserve ratio, asset and liability
                             concentration, to assess and quantify the Company’s overall liquidity risk profile. The Company
                             establishes a liquidity risk limit system, conducts limit management on liquidity risks and monitors
                             and reports the implementation of limits. The Company establishes a quantitative model for
                             the liquidity risk of financial assets and measures the liquidity realisation risk of various types of
                             exchange and over the counter financial assets on a daily basis to assess the liquidity realisation
                             risk of various financial assets.


                             The Company explores and maintains financing channels, continuously keeps an eye on the risk
                             conditions of significant capital providers, and regularly monitors the conditions of significant
                             capital providers’ transactions with the Company. The Company concerns the changes of capital
                             markets, assesses the ability and cost of supplementing its liquidity by issuing stocks, bonds and
                             other financing instruments and mitigates its period mismatch by supplementing its middle-
                             to-long term liquidity. Under the premise of controlling the liquidity risk at the overall level, the
                             Company pays attention to liquidity risk management at various business line levels, to focus
                             on identifying, assessing, monitoring and controlling the fund management business, trading
                             and investment proprietary business, brokerage business, credit business, investment banking
                             business, and liquidity risk factors of the subsidiaries.


                             The Company conducts liquidity risk stress tests on a regular or ad hoc basis by providing
                             simulated environment under extreme liquidity pressures where losses may occur, so as to assess
                             and evaluate the Company’s ability to withstand risks and fulfill its payment obligations in extreme
                             situations, and takes necessary measures to respond to the results reached in the test.




92   GUOTAI HAITONG SECURITIES CO., LTD.
           Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

      The Company establishes and continuously improves the contingency plan for liquidity risks,
      which includes taking measures such as transferring, decentralizing and reducing risks exposure
      to reduce the level of liquidity risks. The Company also establishes emergency response or standby
      systems, procedures and measures for natural disasters, system failures and other emergencies
      so as to reduce losses and reputation damage that the Company may suffer. The contingency
      plan will be rehearsed and assessed regularly, and emergency response arrangements will be
      continually updated and improved.


      Throughout the year of 2025, the liquidity of the market was generally reasonable and sufficient.
      The Company managed to effectively address liquidity shocks at critical times. The Company’s
      liquidity coverage ratio and net stable funding ratio met the regulatory requirement. The net size
      of the daily average cash management pool was higher than the minimum scale limit set by the
      Company and the overall liquidity was in good condition.


(4)   Operational risks


      Operational risks are those that may cause a loss to the Company by failures of internal systems
      and procedures, error or misconduct by employees, fault or failure of information systems or the
      influence of external events.


      The Company sorts out the key risk points and control processes of each business, manages
      daily operational risks by using the operational risk management system, and establishes the self-
      evaluating procedure of operational risk and control. Each department, branch and subsidiary
      actively identifies operational risks in their internal systems and procedures, employees ’
      conduct and IT systems to ensure that the operational risks in existing and new businesses and
      management are adequately assessed. The Company systematically gathers and organizes
      information of the events of operational risk and loss data, establishes key operational risk
      indicator system and monitors its process, and prepares periodical reports. In terms of significant
      operational risk events, it will provide specific valuation reports to ensure that the operational risk
      situation of the Company can be fully understood in a timely manner, which in turn facilitates the
      decision-making regarding the response to the risks or the initiation of contingency plans.


      The Company continuously strengthens the security of information systems, formulates a
      comprehensive emergency response plan for information security events, and conducts regular
      assessment over the main plan and sub plan of emergency response. It also arranges various
      rehearsals against incidents, disasters and other scenarios that cover all important information
      systems in the headquarters and all branches on an annual basis, and improves, modifies and
      upgrades its system and emergency response plan based on the results of rehearsal and findings
      identified.




                                                                                         ANNUAL REPORT 2025     93
     Section III Management Discussion and Analysis

                             In 2025, the Company’s information technology and operational activities ran smoothly and
                             safely without significant operational risk events. The fault backup and recovery time for each
                             information system emergency rehearsal reached our established goal, which demonstrates that
                             the Company’s critical information system possess the required capabilities in responding to
                             failures and disasters.


                      (5)   Reputational risks


                             Reputational risk refers to the risk of negative perceptions about the Company among investors,
                             issuers, regulators, self-regulatory organizations, the public and the media due to its actions or
                             external events and violations of integrity regulations, professional ethics, business norms and
                             conventions by its staff, thereby damaging its brand value, disadvantaging its normal operation,
                             and even affecting the market stability and social stability.


                             The Company incorporates reputational risk management into a comprehensive risk management
                             system, establishes a reputational risk management mechanism, and sets up a brand center
                             (secondary department) as the leading management department for Company’s reputational risk
                             under the Party and mass work department (Party committee propaganda department), requiring
                             all departments, branches, business offices and subsidiaries to actively and effectively prevent
                             reputational risks and respond to reputational risk events, accurately identify, prudently evaluate,
                             dynamically monitor, timely respond to and manage on a full-process basis the reputational risks
                             in the process of business management, and strive to maintain the Company’s reputation and
                             build a high-quality brand image.


                             In 2025, the Company further improved its reputational risk management works. During the
                             Reporting Period, the Company did not experience any major reputational risk event.

(VI) Other disclosures

    1.   Business innovation during the Reporting Period


         During the Reporting Period, with a client-first approach, the Group comprehensively advanced the
         construction of three customer service systems, refining the strategic layout of key businesses, and
         driving innovative development across all operations to consolidate the competitive advantages of its
         principal businesses. In respect of wealth management business, the Group has developed innovative
         models for services, rolled out ETF trading services and portfolio allocation strategies to expand the
         brand influence of our ETF ecosystem. The investment banking business has successfully launched the
         first GEM inquiry and transfer business for shareholders, pioneered several innovative bond products
         including the advanced manufacturing bonds, Shanghai ’s “ Five Centers ” initiative bonds and the
         “Belt and Road” bonds, pioneered several ABS innovative bond products including integrated rural
         revitalization bonds of the Yangtze River Delta region, low-altitude economy bonds and bonds of 100%
         data asset-backed debts. The institutional business continued to enhance the efficiency of its customer
         management, launched the first “Daohe • Sales Connect” business for wealth management subsidiaries
         of major state-owned banks in China, and pioneered the direct settlement services for securities firms
         engaged in insurance and asset management businesses, launched the first financing business under
         QFI, and pioneered the transaction services for building positions of ETFs in Stock Connect for domestic
         and overseas clients. The FICC business pioneered several innovative bonds of income certificate,
         launched American-style, single shark lock-in profit and binary and automatic redemption profit-taking
         structures. It has also completed the first CCER Certified Emission Reduction Registration and Issuance,
         and driving innovative development in carbon finance. The equity business has been actively developing
         various QIS strategy indexes. Among which, a full-replication tracking product of “CSI Guotai Haitong
         Securities Dynamic Allocation Index on Major Asset Categories (中證國泰海通證券大類資產動態配置
         指數)” has been launched. We also successfully launched the cross-border return swap business linked
         with the targets in the Canadian market. The investment management business actively promoted
         product innovation. Hua An Fund issued the first tranche of benchmark-linked floating-fee products. The
         Guotai Haitong Asset Management issued the first asset-backed mutual REITs for municipal heating in
         China, and Guotai Junan Innovation Investment successfully launched the first private equity secondary
         market fund. In respect of international business, the Company supported commercial banks in the
         Middle East in establishment and trading of the first QFI stock product of the PRC. It has also supported
         the issuance of “ Yulan Bonds (玉蘭債)”, the first bond issued by a privately owned enterprise in the
         world.

     The Company keeps improving its corporate governance structure and system in order to enhance its corporate
     governance.

     According to the requirements of laws, regulations and regulatory documents such as the Company Law (《公司法》     ),
                        《證券法》
     the Securities Law (          ), the Regulations on Supervision and Administration of Securities Companies (《證
     券公司監督管理條例》             ), the Rules for Governance of Securities Companies (《證券公司治理準則》            ) and the Code
     of Corporate Governance for Listed Companies (    《上市公司治理準則》            ), the Company has established a sound
     and complete corporate governance structure, comprising the general meeting, the Board (and the four special
     committees under the Board), and the management of the Company to form a complete corporate governance
     system for discussion, decision-making, delegation and implementation with clear responsibilities, regulated
     operation, coordination and balance among the competent authorities, the decision making body, the supervision
     body and management.

     The Directors of the Company believe that good corporate governance is crucial to maintaining effective corporate
     operations, establishing a comprehensive corporate culture, realizing sound business development and protecting
     long-term shareholders ’ value. Therefore, the Company has been practicing a high standard of corporate
     governance.

     During the Reporting Period, the Company has strictly complied with the relevant provisions under the Corporate
     Governance Code and satisfied most requirements of provisions for recommended best practices. During the
     Reporting Period, the Company has amended the Articles of Association and certain policies; the Chairman of
     the Company has communicated with non-executive Directors via various channels such as meetings to obtain

           AFFECT THE COMPANY’S INDEPENDENCE

           The controlling shareholders and de facto controllers of the Company have established a relatively sound corporate
           governance structure and business operation system to ensure the independence of the Company’ s assets,
           personnel, finance, organization, business, etc. In terms of assets, both parties have their own independent business
           premises and do not have joint offices or mixed assets, and the ownership of assets is clear; in terms of personnel,
           the management and business teams of both parties are completely separated and do not have concurrent posts,
           and have independent and complete systems for labor relations, labor contracts, personnel, wage management
           and social insurance, etc.; in terms of finance, both parties have established independent financial and accounting
           institutions, with independent accounting budgets, accounting systems and financial management systems,
           independent bank accounts and independent tax payments and no financial personnel holding concurrent posts
           in the Company; in terms of institutions, both parties have established an independent and complete business
           system and an independent administrative management system, and there is no administrative affiliation between
           each functional organization and the Company; in terms of business, both parties have established an independent
           business operation mechanism.

            Explanations:


            1.    The term of office of Directors and senior management members re-elected shall commence on the date on which they first
                  assume office.


            2.    On 3 April 2025, the Resolution on the Election of the Non-Independent Directors of the seventh session of the Board and the
                  Resolution on Election of the Independent Directors of the seventh session of the Board of the Company were considered and
                  approved at the 2025 first extraordinary general meeting, and Mr. ZHU Jian, Mr. LI Junjie, Mr. NIE Xiaogang, Mr. ZHOU Jie, Ms.
                  GUAN Wei, Mr. ZHONG Maojun, Mr. CHEN Hangbiao, Ms. LV Chunfang, Ms. HA Erman, Mr. SUN Minghui and Mr. CHEN Yijiang
                  were elected as non-independent directors of the seventh session of the Board, among whom Mr. ZHU Jian, Mr. LI Junjie, Ms.
                  GUAN Wei, Mr. ZHONG Maojun, Mr. SUN Minghui and Mr. CHEN Yijiang were re-appointed. Mr. LI Renjie, Mr. WANG Guogang,
                  Mr. PU Yonghao, Mr. MAO Fugen, Mr. CHEN Fangruo and Mr. JIANG Xian were elected as the independent Directors of seventh
                  session of the Board, among whom Mr. LI Renjie, Mr. WANG Guogang and Mr. PU Yonghao were re-elected. The foregoing
                  Directors shall perform their duties from the date of resolution at the general meeting on 3 April 2025. Mr. LIU Xinyi, Mr. CHEN
                  Hua, Mr. ZHANG Manhua, Mr. WANG Tao, Mr. DING Wei, Mr. BAI Wei and Mr. YIM Chi Hung Henry, the Directors of the sixth
                  session of the Board, ceased to be the Directors of the Company.


            3.    On 3 April 2025, the Company convened the first meeting of the seventh session of the Board, at which the Resolution on Electing
                  the Chairman and Vice Chairman of the Seventh Session of the Board of the Company《關於提請選舉公司第七屆董事會董事
                  長、副董事長的議案》was considered and approved. Mr. ZHU Jian was elected as the chairman of the seventh session of the
                  Board of the Company. Mr. ZHOU Jie was elected as the vice chairman of the seventh session of the Board of the Company. Mr. LI
                  Junjie ceased to be the vice chairman of the Board of the Company.


            4.    On 3 July 2025, Mr. WU Hongwei was elected as an employee Director of the seventh session of the Board at the seventh meeting of
                  the fifth session of the employees’ representative assembly of the Company and has performed his duties as the Director for a term
                  consistent with the term of office of the seventh session of the Board, the commencement date is the date of his election.


            5.    On 3 April 2025, the Company convened the first meeting of the seventh session of the Board, at which the Resolution on
                  Appointing the Senior Management of the Company《關於提請聘任公司高級管理人員的議案》was considered and approved,
                  pursuant to which, Mr. LI Junjie was appointed as the President of the Company, and Mr. MAO Yuxing, Mr. XIE Lebin, Mr. LUO
                  Dongyuan, Mr. NIE Xiaogang, Mr. PAN Guangtao, Mr. ZHANG Xinjun, Mr. CHEN Zhongyi and Mr. HAN Zhida were appointed
                  as the vice presidents of the Company. Mr. NIE Xiaogang concurrently served as the secretary to the Board and chief risk officer
                  of the Company, Mr. ZHANG Xinjun concurrently served as the chief financial officer of the Company, and Mr. ZHAO Hong also
                  served as the chief auditor of the Company. Mr. YU Feng was appointed as the chief information officer of the Company, and Ms.
                  ZHAO Huiwen was appointed as the chief compliance officer (to be formally performed upon obtaining regulatory approval) and
                  the chief legal counsel of the Company. Among them, Mr. LI Junjie, Mr. XIE Lebin, Mr. LUO Dongyuan, Mr. NIE Xiaogang, Mr.
                  CHEN Zhongyi, Mr. HAN Zhida and Mr. ZHAO Hong as senior management appointed by the sixth session of the Board were
                  reappointed by the seventh session of the Board; Mr. MAO Yuxing, Mr. PAN Guangtao, Mr. ZHANG Xinjun, Mr. YU Feng and Ms.
                  ZHAO Huiwen were the senior management newly appointed by the seventh session of the Board. The term of office of the above
                  senior management is consistent with the term of office of the seventh session of the Board. Mr. NIE Xiaogang ceased to be the chief
                  financial officer of the Company, and Ms. ZHANG Zhihong ceased to serve as the chief compliance officer and chief legal counsel of
                  the Company.


            6.    On 22 May 2025, the appointment of Ms. ZHAO Huiwen as the chief compliance officer of the Company was approved by the
                  relevant local office of the CSRC, and she officially took the position of the chief compliance officer of the Company on the same
                  date.

      ZUO Zhipeng, SHAO Liangming and XIE Min, all members of the sixth session of the Supervisory Committee, ceased to serve as

      Director with effect from 27 March 2026.
